# Problem 2 
## Import and Tidy
```{r}
nhanes1_df = read_csv(file = "./nhanes_covar.csv", skip = 4, na = c("NA", "", "."))|>
    janitor::clean_names()|>
mutate(sex = factor(sex, 
                    levels = c("1","2"), 
                    labels = c("male", "female")), 
       education = factor(education, 
                          levels = c("1", "2", "3"), 
                          labels = c("less than high school", "equivalent to high school","more than high school"))
       )|>
  filter(age>=21)
```

```{r}
nhanes2_df = read_csv(file = "./nhanes_accel.csv", na = c("NA", "", "."))|>
  janitor::clean_names()
```
## Join
```{r}
fullnhanes_df = left_join(nhanes1_df, nhanes2_df)
```
## Table & Visualization of Education by Sex 
```{r}
fullnhanes_df |>
  count(sex,education)|>
  pivot_wider (names_from = sex, 
               values_from = n, 
               values_fill = 0
  )
```
```{r}
fullnhanes_df |>
  ggplot (aes(x = age, fill = sex)) +
  geom_histogram(position = "dodge", binwidth = 2)+
facet_wrap (~education)+
  labs(
    title = "Age Distribution for Males and Females Across Education Levels", 
    x = "Age (years)", 
    y = "Count", 
    color = "Sex"
  )+
theme (legend.position = "bottom")
```
The "more than high school" education level has a larger count of participants than the other two levels. While "more than high school" and "less than high school" had relatively the same number of males and females in them, the "equivalent to high school" had 13 less female participants than male. Particpant's ages were distributed across 20 to 80 years, with most ages having one or two participants at that age. The "more than high school" education level had more ages that had more than two participants than the other two education levels.

## total activity
```{r}

fullnhanes_df = fullnhanes_df |>
  mutate(total_activity = rowSums(across(starts_with("min"))))
```

## Total Activity Visualization

```{r}
fullnhanes_df |>
  ggplot(aes (x = age, y = total_activity, color = sex))+
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5)+
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE, method = "lm")+
  facet_wrap(~education)+
  labs(
    title = "Total Activity by Age and Sex Across Education Levels", 
    x = "Age (years)", 
    y = "Total Activity in MIMS", 
    color = "Sex"
  )+
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Total activity demonstrates large variablity across sex and age; however, there is a general trend across education levels to decrease across age. This is most pronounced in the "less than high school" level, particularly for females, while this much less pronouncced in the "more than high school" level. 

## 24-hour Activity 
```{r}
fullnhanes_df |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("min"),
    names_to = "minutes", 
    names_prefix = "min", 
    values_to = "activity"
  )|>
  mutate (minutes = as.numeric(minutes))|>
  
  ggplot(aes(x = minutes, y = activity, color= sex))+
  geom_line (aes(group = sex), alpha = 0.3)+
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE, linewidth = 0.5)+
  facet_wrap(~education, ncol = 1)+
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0,1440, by = 240), 
    labels = c("12:00am", "4:00am", "8:00am", "12:00pm", "4:00pm", "8:00pm", "11:59pm")
  )+
  labs (
    title = "24-Hour Activity by Sex and Education Level", 
    x = "Time of Day",
    y = "Activity", 
    color = "Sex"
  )+
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

From these graphs, activity begins increasing around 6-7 hours after the start wear, which is consistent with the data starting at midnight and thus participants are likely sleeping up until 6 or 7 in the morning and then begin their day, leading to increased activity levels. Activity decreases are also noted to start around 10pm, or hour 22 of wear, consistent with common sleep cycles. There appears to be more male activity across typical sleeping hours in the "less than high school" education level, which could be indicative of nightshift work in this population. There is also a pattern of high activity in males in the "more than high school" education level that is impacting the graphs, which might be indicative of afterwork activity with this population. 

# Problem 3 

```{r}
jan20_df = read_csv(file = "./Jan 2020 Citi.csv") |>
  janitor::clean_names()|>
  mutate(month = c("jan"), 
         year = c("2020"),
         rideable_type = as.factor(rideable_type), 
         weekdays = as.factor(weekdays), 
         start_station_name = as.factor(start_station_name),
         end_station_name = as.factor(end_station_name), 
         member_casual = as.factor(member_casual))
  
jan24_df = read_csv(file = "./Jan 2024 Citi.csv")|>
  janitor::clean_names()|>
   mutate(month = c("jan"), 
         year = c("2024"),
         rideable_type = as.factor(rideable_type), 
         weekdays = as.factor(weekdays), 
         start_station_name = as.factor(start_station_name),
         end_station_name = as.factor(end_station_name), 
         member_casual = as.factor(member_casual))

july20_df = read_csv(file = "./July 2020 Citi.csv")|>
  janitor:: clean_names()|>
  mutate(month = c("july"), 
         year = c("2020"),
         rideable_type = as.factor(rideable_type), 
         weekdays = as.factor(weekdays), 
         start_station_name = as.factor(start_station_name),
         end_station_name = as.factor(end_station_name), 
         member_casual = as.factor(member_casual))

july24_df = read_csv(file = "./July 2024 Citi.csv")|>
  janitor::clean_names()|>
   mutate(month = c("july"), 
         year = c("2024"),
         rideable_type = as.factor(rideable_type), 
         weekdays = as.factor(weekdays), 
         start_station_name = as.factor(start_station_name),
         end_station_name = as.factor(end_station_name), 
         member_casual = as.factor(member_casual))

citifull_df = bind_rows(jan20_df, jan24_df, july20_df, july24_df)|>
  mutate(month = as.factor(month), 
          year = as.factor(year))
```
## Table 1
```{r}
citifull_df|>
count(month, year, member_casual)|>
  pivot_wider(names_from = member_casual, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)
  
```
Members had more rides across all months and years than casual riders. The use of Citi Bike by both members and casual riders has grown since 2020. 

## Table 2

```{r}
citifull_df|>
  filter(year == "2024", month == "july")|>
  count(start_station_name, sort = TRUE) |>
  slice_head(n=5)|>
 knitr:: kable(col.names=c("Starting station", "number of rides"),
   caption = "Five most popular starting stations in July 2024")
```
